chunks: Ali from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will gather the first and the last in one plain. Then a caller will call out: 'Where are the people of merit?'

So a group of people will stand, and the angels will meet them and say: 'And what was your merit?' So they will say: 'We maintained relations with those who cut us off, and we gave to those who deprived us, and we pardoned those who oppressed us.'
He said: 'So it will be said to them: You have spoken the truth. Enter Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What defines the 'people of merit' who are called out on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the concept of 'Fadl' (excellence) not as ritualistic piety alone, but as active moral reciprocity, specifically pardoning those who wronged you. This aligns with the Shia emphasis on 'Iffah' (chastity of character) and social harmony, where the 'people of merit' are distinguished by their ability to transcend personal grievance. The scene underscores that divine validation of such ethical conduct leads directly to Paradise, reinforcing the practical application of Quranic virtues in daily interactions.
